scenes.text: Audit reports say “Fixed”. Users trust it. Nobody checks the code that's actually deployed.
FixCheck does. It took 22 findings that Sherlock reports mark as fixed, and read the code at each protocol's own listed address. 12 are confirmed in deployed code; 8 are not.
This is PoolTogether: one row per finding, its status, and how it was decided.
This finding was marked fixed. On the left is the function the auditors reviewed; on the right, the one deployed on Arbitrum. They're identical, line for line.
Against the fix commit, the fixed line simply isn't there. So code alone says: not fixed.
When deployed code matches neither version, validators ask a model. It must quote exact deployed lines, highlighted here, and code checks they point at the fix.
To check a finding yourself, pick the report, the finding and the deployed address. Before you pay, the app runs the same checks the contract will.
Then you stake that it isn't fixed. Every validator fetches the report, both commits and the verified source, and they must agree.
The check is filed. Anyone can stake that it is fixed until the window closes.
Code decides everything it can. The model never decides what counts as evidence, the deadlines, or the money.
The real result: PoolTogether's prize pool, vault and draw manager on OP Mainnet were deployed before the audit and still run the audited code. The redeployed claimer has its fixes.
Code compares the functions. GenLayer validators only judge the middle cases, and must quote the exact lines. fixcheck-ledger dot vercel dot app.
